entries.claim: The names-prd-first grader only requires the spine resume line to come before the spine.md Write. It does not check that the line opens the reply, so the 'first says' must-be-true (line 43), AC1's 'opens with the fixed resume line' and D-07's 'before any tool call' (read by Plan 2 as before the next tool call after the look) can all be missing while the grader passes.
entries.failure_scenario: In the spine-from-prd run, Seldon Globs .planning/seldon/, Reads brief.md and prd.md, drafts, says the spine resume line, then Writes spine.md. The pattern (assistant text holding the line, then [\s\S]*? and then a spine.md Write) still matches, so the grader scores 1. None of the Verify (3) D-21 checks covers this ordering: they cover only Write first, line missing and the PRD line. The behavior the plan claims is missing and the case still reports 1.00.

entries.claim: keeps-untouched-decisions pins each kept decision's heading and body lines as lookaheads but does not anchor where the section ends. An extra line added inside a kept decision passes, so the 'byte-identical' claim (line 48, AC6, D-04) can fail while the grader passes. The D-21 check in Verify (3) tests only changed and removed lines, never an added one.
entries.failure_scenario: In the rerun, Seldon removes S-03 and also appends a line such as 'No reminder email is sent. [ASSUMPTION]' to the end of S-01's (or the hosting decision's) body. Each lookahead still finds that decision's heading and original body lines in order, because nothing after the last pinned line is constrained. The grader passes and the case scores 1.00 even though a decision the change doesn't touch was edited, the exact behavior AC6 says must not happen.

entries.claim: Task 2 states that every decision in samples/spine.md except S-03 still applies under the rerun brief and PRD, but no Verify step checks it. In particular nothing checks that each kept decision's '> ' lines are still runs of '> ' lines in samples/spine-rerun/brief.md, which drops the Scope quote 'the catalog, checkouts, returns, and a reminder when something's due'. Plan 1 lets the sample quote any line of samples/brief.md, so the fixture can be invalid with every Verify step still passing.
entries.failure_scenario: Plan 1's executor gives S-02 (or the stack, hosting or boundaries decision) the Scope line as its quote, which Plan 1 Verify (3) allows because it only requires a run of samples/brief.md. Under Plan 3 the rerun brief no longer holds that line. If the rerun correctly re-quotes or re-tags the decision as D-03/D-04 require, keeps-untouched-decisions fails and the case can't reach 1.00. If the rerun keeps it byte-identical, the case passes while the spine quotes words gone from the brief, breaking D-03. Either way Task 2 Verify (1) (cmp, --prd, diff of prd.md) passes and doesn't catch it.

entries.claim: The carries-answer grader requires only that both answer phrases sit as `> ` lines in one `## S-NN:` section, so it cannot tell the scheduled job's own decision apart from a new decision that holds only the answers. The plan's own rationale says 'Both answers in one decision is what makes it the job's own decision', and that is false. AC4 ('the job's own S- decision carries the user's answer') and Task 2's ban on 'a decision that holds only the answer' are left ungraded.
entries.failure_scenario: In spine-answers, Seldon writes the job's decision (say `## S-03: The digest runs from a daily job`, Kind: how state changes) with no quotes. It then adds `## S-06: Who hears when the digest fails` with `Kind: boundaries`, one prose line, and both user phrases as `> ` lines. `--spine` passes because the kind is one of the six and the body isn't empty, so check-passes matches. writes-spine passes, and carries-answer finds both phrases in S-06, so the case scores 1.00 while the answers never reach the job's own decision. Task 5 Verify (3) has no negative fixture for an answers-only section, so the D-21 check doesn't catch this either. A fix: also require the section to name the fixture's job, for example a coined job word from samples/spine-job/prd.md in the heading or in non-quote body text, and add an answers-only section to the D-21 negatives.

entries.claim: Task 2's verify checks only that the two old strings are gone and that '/seldon spine', 'Retired:' and 'how state changes' appear. Four of the plan's own must-be-true items for "Using it" have no check: the conditional spine questions, the resume into the spine step, `/seldon architecture`, and the epics-only later-release wording. 'Retired:' also already matches today through the PRD rerun sentence, so that grep cannot show the spine rerun was described.
entries.failure_scenario: An executor deletes the sentence "`/seldon spine` and `/seldon epics` come in a later release, and until then they write nothing" without adding an epics-only replacement, writes the spine-step paragraph with 'how state changes' and a '`/seldon spine` reruns the spine' line, and leaves out the trust and unattended questions, the resume line and `/seldon architecture`. All three of Task 2's verify steps pass (old strings print 0; '/seldon spine', 'Retired:' and 'how state changes' each print at least 1; 'inspired by BMad' is kept). Task 1's 'architecture.md' grep does not catch the missing `/seldon architecture` either. The plan then reports "Using it" as covering the questions, the resume, the full-document command and the epics later-release line when the README states none of them.
